analysis.purpose: runCli is a test helper that invokes the local CLI binary in a real repository with the provided arguments and returns the trimmed stdout as a string. It gives tests a synchronous, black-box way to exercise the CLI entry point and assert on its textual output.
responsibilities: Spawn the CLI script as a child process using the current Node executable
Run in the configured test repository working directory
Capture stdout (and stderr) into a 32 MB buffer and return the trimmed stdout

inputs.name: args
inputs.description: CLI arguments to pass after the script path

outputs.name: stdout
outputs.description: Trimmed standard output of the CLI process

sideEffects: Spawns a synchronous child process via execFileSync
Reads up to 32 MB of combined output into memory
errorBehavior: Does not catch execFileSync failures; any non-zero exit or spawn error propagates to the caller as an exception
invariants: Always returns the stdout string with leading and trailing whitespace removed
preconditions: The CLI script at path `CLI` must be executable by `process.execPath`
The test repository `repo` must exist and be accessible
postconditions: The child process has terminated and its stdout is returned
risks: Large output could exceed the 32 MB maxBuffer and crash the helper
Unresolved call to Node built-in execFileSync means exact behavior is not modeled in the graph
whatToDistrust: execFileSync and trim are unresolved built-in calls; exact error semantics and trimming behavior are assumed from Node.js documentation, not from indexed code
CLI constant is not shown in the seed; actual script path is external to this symbol

nodes.name: CLI test runner
nodes.summary: Synchronous black-box invocation of the CLI binary for test assertions
